scope: main-experiment mechanism rigor (steering-coefficient sweep, check A)

A_coefficient_sweep.note: Unit (raw additive multiplier on fixed-norm direction; alpha=16 ~ 1.2x block-26 mean act-norm), capability logging (ORF-valid, loglik, %E, GC at every alpha), 32x geometric sweep with alpha=0 baseline, and norm-matched random-direction control are all adequate. Run MET its pass criterion at alpha=16 so a wider sweep is not required; HOWEVER %H was still rising at the max tested alpha with no plateau/mid-plateau lock, and the coincident GC collapse + loglik change leave the off-target compositional shift incompletely disentangled.

key_findings: Sweep covered 32x nonzero-alpha range, >=5 nonzero points, alpha=0 included.
Capability/coherence metrics logged at every alpha.
Norm-matched random-direction control swept; did not reproduce the effect.
Run met its pass criterion at alpha=16 (failure-to-sweep-wide N/A).
Effect still increasing at alpha=16; no demonstrated plateau or locked mid-plateau setting.
rationale: Adequate coefficient calibration, metric logging, geometric coverage, and a relevant random-direction control; criterion achieved, so absence of a wider post-success sweep is not a failure. But the effect is unsaturated at the largest alpha (no stable plateau) and the concurrent GC/loglik shifts are an incompletely disentangled compositional confound -> WARN, not PASS.
